The available evidence suggests that concomitant anterior/apical repair during midurethral sling does not result in additional improvement in overactive bladder (OAB) symptoms compared to midurethral sling alone. Studies have shown that while concomitant AA repair may be associated with shorter operative times and reduced postoperative complications, it does not lead to significant improvements in OAB symptoms.

In fact, patients who underwent concomitant AA repair experienced a similar reduction in OAB symptoms as those who received midurethral sling alone. Additionally, the presence of posterior wall slippage during midurethral sling repair is thought to be a major contributor to the development of overactive bladder symptoms, and concomitant AA repair may not address this underlying issue.

Therefore, while concomitant anterior/apical repair during midurethral sling may have benefits in terms of reduced operative time and complication rates, it does not improve OAB symptoms as effectively as midurethral sling alone.
